previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever and neutropenia eight days after high-dose Cytoxan for stem cell mobilization in the setting of multiple myeloma. He presented with somnolence, attributed to recent narcotic and Xanax use, and was found to have very low white blood cell and platelet counts. He was treated with IV cefepime, later broadened to vancomycin due to persistent fevers, though all cultures remained negative. Imaging showed mild bronchiolitis, likely viral, and no bacterial source was identified. His neutrophil count gradually recovered, fevers resolved, and IV antibiotics were discontinued in favor of oral levofloxacin. A tunneled pheresis catheter was placed on discharge day, and his first stem cell collection was successfully completed. He was discharged home in stable, afebrile condition to continue daily pheresis sessions and oral antibiotic therapy.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male w/CAD, HTN, paroxismal afib, COPD, history of 
bladder CA (s/p resection and neobladder formation) and multiple 
myeloma s/p velcade and revlimid, who was admitted for auto SCT. 
Hospital course by problem:
.  
# Multiple Myeloma- The patient is s/p 6 cycles of 
Velcade+dexamethasone and Revlimid regimen, s/p cell collection 
___ for 86 million cells. He had a temporary CVL placed. He 
was treated with melphalan and lasix per protocol on d-3 and 
d-2. Acyclovir and cipro ppx were started d-1. Day ___. He 
received neupogen after SCT and was non-neutropenic on ___. 
Overall he tolerated the treatment well, though he suffered from 
neutropenic fevers and mucositis/esophagitis around his nadir, 
which improved as his counts recovered. 
.  
# Fever/neutropenia- He spiked a fever on ___ with no 
localizing symptoms, and antibiotics were switched from cipro to 
cefepime. On ___ he spiked again and developed a new cough with 
brown sputum, as well as some difficulty swallowing. He aso had 
some LLQ TTP. Initially there was concern for pneumonia (also 
aspiration), ___, and typhlitis, so he was 
started on vanc, fluconazol, and flagyl on ___.  Portable CXR 
suggested the beginning of a R sided PNA but follow up chest CT 
was negative for lung pathology. CT chest did, however, show 
esophagitis and L sided hydronephrosis. He spiked again on ___, 
so fluconazole was changed to caspo for broader fungal coverage. 
He was afebrile on ___, and his counts began to recover. He was 
non-neutropenic on ___ so vanc/flagyl were stopped and on ___  
caspo/cefepime were stopped, as no organisms had been isolated. 
He remained afebrile and clinically improved as his counts 
recovered.  He did grow VRE in his urine but given this was 
asymptomatic and there were less than 100,000 colonies, this was 
felt to be colonization, which is common with the neobladder, 
and upon discussion with infectious disease, it was felt he did 
not need to be treated for this. He should have a follow up U/A 
culture 1 week after discharge to ensure there is no progression 
from colonization to infection.
.  
# History of bladder CA, neobladder/urinary retention: On past 
admissions the patient needed to be straight cathed due to 
retension. He had increased urinary frequency and abdominal 
distension a slightly increased Cr during his nadir. He was 
started on pyrimidine x3days ___ with little effect. PVR was 
1L. CT showed worsened L sided hydronephrosis. The patient is 
s/p L ureteral stricture and reimplantation. Urology was 
consulted and felt the hydronephrosis is likely chronic given 
his anatomy, and retension was likely increased in the setting 
of increased narcotics and bed rest. They recommend q2h voiding 
schedule and once daily straight cath to eval for retention. 
Straight cath in pm of ___ drained 1.6L, in am ___ drained 
1.3L, despite frequent voiding. His Cr has stayed stable and he 
no longer was symptomatic. Per urology, as long as the patient 
is asymptomatic and there is no change in Cr, the patient can 
self-straight cath on a prn basis, when he has symptoms of 
distension. 
.  
# AMS- On ___ the patient was more somnolent with pinpoint 
pupils. This was felt to be due to a combination of receiving 
ativan and increased narcotics, bladder retention in the setting 
of illness. He apparently has had confusion with ativan in the 
past. Head CT was obtained and was negative for bleed. MS 
improved by ___ with decreased oxycontin dose and no further 
ativan administration.  
.  
# ARF- On ___ his Cr increased. Vanc trough in am on ___ was 
high 21.4, so dose was decreased, though vanc was discontinued 
shortly after. Cr improved with straight caths and as his 
retension resolved.  
.  
# Anemia- During his nadir his HCT was not responsive to 
transfusions. This was thought to be due to slow bleed from 
esophagitis- DAT/Ab screen were negative.
.  
# Invasive squamous cell ca- Prior to admission he had these 
excised from his L forearm. These were monitored in house. He 
should have follow up with dermatology as an outpatient given 
how close the cancer was to the border of the exisions.
.  
# Fingertip peeling- The patient developed some peeling of skin 
on his fingers which appeared to be dry skin, not c/w ___ 
___. This resolved with moisturizer.  
.  
# Back pain/spinal stenosis- On admission the patient was 
continued on his home pain regimen of oxycontin 20mg BID with 
prn 10mg oxycodone. He required increasing amounts of medication 
so his oxycontin was increased to 30mg BID to keep pain well 
controlled. However, this was decreased back to 20mg BID given 
AMS as above. 
.  
#. CAD - s/p MI in ___ with RCA stenting, EF 50% and clean 
coronaries ___  
Not on ASA, BB; may benefit from an ASA from a survival 
standpoint after stabilized from transplant but not started now 
given risk of bleeding ___.  
.  
# Atrial fibrillation- Had been on anticoagulation with coumadin 
at home but stopped ___ due to autologous transplant; cont to 
hold coumadin ___. Admission EKG showed sinus 
rhythm, mild 1st degree AVB, repeated ___ was unchanged. Restart

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital for an autologous stem cell 
transplant. You received the treatment and stem cell reinfusion 
according to protocol. You developed a fever while you were 
neutropenic, and you were treated with broad spectrum 
antibiotics, but no source of infection was isolated. Your 
antibiotics were stopped once you were no longer neutropenic.
.
Your urine grew vancomycin resistent enterococcus (VRE) but this 
likely represents colonization rather than a true infection and 
therefore does not need to be treated with antibiotics. You 
should have your urine rechecked in 1 week.
.
Please take acyclovir for prophylaxis. You received aerosolized 
pentamidine on your last day in the hospital. Please take 
bactrim when you are told by your doctor to start.
.
Your magnesium was low so you should take 400mg magnesium twice 
a day, unless told to stop by your doctor. It is very important 
you drink lots of fluids (2 liters/day). If you notice you are 
not urinating well or feel you are retaining fluid you should 
straight cath yourself as instructed by your urologists.
.
Please do not take coumadin until instructed by Dr. ___.
.
If you develop fever, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, 
inability to eat or drink, increased diarrhea, pain when you 
urinate, or any other concerning symptoms, please call the 
clinic.
